editorial.headline: Wholesale Sewing Supplies: Nationally Open, Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale sewing supplies carry a fully open national foreign-investment position, but Bali’s risk-class moratorium makes PMA registration unavailable on the island.
editorial.body:
KBLI 46415 covers the wholesale trade in sewing supplies: needles, sewing thread and zippers. The category’s scope is deliberately concrete. Its examples identify the things being traded, preventing the activity from becoming a catch-all description for every commercial undertaking connected with textiles or clothing. The relevant business is wholesale dealing in the stated sewing supplies. For registration purposes, its identity begins with that exact, practical inventory: needles, thread and zippers.

Nationally, the activity is marked TERBUKA. It is open to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. The record also admits every listed scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That pairing gives the national position its full shape. The activity is not confined in the record to a single scale, and the foreign-ownership ceiling is not a partial stake. At the national level, founders can read the category as open across those stated scales with full foreign ownership permitted up to the recorded maximum.

Bali produces the decisive qualification. A foreign investor cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The Bali classification is blocked by risk class. Its recorded reason is precise: at the Besar scale, OSS assigns every scope a Low or Medium-Low risk outcome. Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA registration. The record places this moratorium in May 2026. This is a direct registration block, not a Bali-side adjustment to the national 100% ceiling.

The national and Bali readings should be kept in their proper jurisdictions. Nationally, the record says TERBUKA and permits a foreign stake of up to 100%; in Bali, the moratorium supplies the present PMA outcome. Neither statement cancels the other. The useful conclusion is exact rather than optimistic: wholesale sewing supplies remain the defined activity, the national status is open at every listed scale, and Bali is unavailable for a PMA registration because of the recorded risk-class rule. That is the distinction an investment decision must respect.
